chapter: The jazz war with Leonard Feather
title: Young Women of America and the Robeson riot
summary: Another left-wing group hired him, then advertised a Paul Robeson concert that ended in a riot. Hodes tore up the contract and the jobs stopped.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: Obnoxious, I don't know who they are, but they give me a deposit, a union contract. They hire me and I got Max Kqminsky and I got Chippy Hill, I got -- and I go to the newspapers and I get a plug in the columns. In a week, I see an ad in the paper: The Young Women of America who so success-
fully produced the Paul Robeson concert in New Jersey. That was a riot in New Jersey, that concert. It was a big riot and a lot of problems.
It came out that Robeson was a Communist.

Was a Communist. And it really caused a stink. So I went to the same writers of the newspapers, and I told them what had happened. And I says, as far as I'm concerned, there's the contract, and I tore it up, I will not be there. And that's how I broke with them. They stopped giving me jobs. But they were really on my tail.
